back: The single, tenant-wide, SaaS data lake built into every Fabric tenant. All workloads store data here in Delta/Parquet format so items can share data without copying it.
A logical grouping of workspaces by business area, used to apply consistent governance, ownership, and discoverability policies.
A Fabric feature that assigns workspaces to Development/Test/Production stages and lets you compare and push content between them in a controlled way.
An Azure-billed Fabric capacity (pay-as-you-go or reserved) that can be scaled, paused, and resumed, and supports all Fabric workloads.
Connects a workspace to a branch in Azure DevOps or GitHub for source control, commit history, and pull-request review of workspace items.
An AppSource app that visualizes CU utilization, throttling, and smoothing for a Fabric capacity over time.
A centralized, cross-workspace view of activity such as pipeline runs, refreshes, and job status.
Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer — control what a user can do inside a workspace, from full management (Admin) to read-only interaction (Viewer).
Tenant-wide switches controlling which features and capabilities (like trial capacities) are enabled, often scoped to specific security groups.
Stops or restarts billing and compute for an F SKU capacity on demand, without losing any content, useful for cost control during idle periods.
A low-code, Power Query-based ETL item for ingesting and transforming data, able to output directly into a Lakehouse or Warehouse.
Lakehouse: Spark-managed Delta tables with a read-only SQL endpoint. Warehouse: full T-SQL engine with transactions, stored procedures, and views.
A reference from OneLake to data stored elsewhere (ADLS Gen2, S3, another Fabric item) that lets you read it in place without copying it.
Continuous, near real-time replication of an external operational database into Delta tables in OneLake, without building custom pipelines.
A write-time optimization that sorts and encodes Parquet files for faster reads by Power BI and SQL engines.
Compacts many small files in a Delta table into fewer, larger files to improve read performance.
Removes data files no longer referenced by the Delta transaction log and older than the retention threshold, reclaiming storage.
Physically splitting a large table (often by date) so query engines can skip irrelevant partitions and scan less data.
Bronze = raw source data. Silver = cleansed, conformed, validated data. Gold = business-level, aggregated, reporting-ready data.
A read-only T-SQL endpoint automatically generated for every Lakehouse, letting you query Delta tables without writing Spark code.
A model design with a central fact table (measures/events) surrounded by dimension tables (descriptive attributes), recommended for performance and DAX compatibility.
Measure: evaluated dynamically in the current filter context at query time. Calculated column: computed once per row at refresh time and stored in the model.
Data is copied into the semantic model's in-memory cache and refreshed on a schedule; fast queries, but data can be stale between refreshes.
Queries are sent to the source system live at report run time; always current, but subject to source system performance and latency.
Reads Delta Parquet files directly from OneLake into memory on demand, combining near-Import performance with no traditional refresh step.
Exposes a semantic model over the standard analytical protocol so external tools (Tabular Editor, third-party BI tools) can read, and optionally write, model objects.
A refresh policy that partitions a table by date range and only reprocesses recent, changing partitions instead of the whole table.
Roles defined with DAX filter expressions (often using USERPRINCIPALNAME()) that restrict which rows a signed-in user can see in a report.
A Power BI project file format that stores reports and semantic models as human-readable folders/files (TMDL for the model), suited for Git source control.
A Power BI Desktop tool that records how long each visual takes for DAX query execution and rendering, used to diagnose slow reports.
The query language used against KQL databases in an Eventhouse, optimized for fast, ad hoc exploration of large-scale time-series and event data.
The KQL operator that groups rows and computes aggregates per group, analogous to GROUP BY plus aggregate functions in SQL.
The KQL operator that merges rows from two tables based on a matching key, similar to a SQL JOIN.
A code-first item running on Spark compute, supporting PySpark/Spark SQL/Scala/R, used for exploratory analysis and large-scale transformation.
An RDL-based report type designed for pixel-perfect, print-ready layouts such as invoices, unlike interactive Power BI reports.
A dashboard built from KQL querysets over Eventhouse data, designed to visualize streaming data with automatic, low-latency updates.
A Power BI Desktop view for writing and running DAX queries directly against a model and seeing tabular results, without building visuals.
AI assistance integrated across Fabric items (notebooks, Data Factory, Power BI, Real-Time Intelligence) that generates code, queries, summaries, and reports from natural-language prompts.
A Fabric capability that monitors data (including streaming data) for defined conditions and automatically triggers actions like Teams or email alerts.
A Fabric item for capturing, transforming, and routing real-time streaming data (e.g., into an Eventhouse or Lakehouse) without writing custom ingestion code.
